answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to periodically pass a randomized capability benchmark: a fresh task graded against a rubric, with scores published on-chain. A farm running a thousand identities from one model produces near-identical outputs, so statistical fingerprints merge them into one. To fake independence, the attacker must run a thousand distinct models, each with real inference cost. Honest agents pass with work they already do, like a wharf admitting only ships with real cargo, while an ember of doubt at the zenith triggers a retest before reward.
